title: Retargeting Video Ad Template | AIVideosUGC
description: Win back shoppers who viewed a product or left a cart with a retargeting video from one photo. Set audience, offer and frequency in your ad platform.
h1: Retargeting Video Ads for a Second Look
lead: Most shoppers leave after viewing a product and never return, yet reusing the same ad creative does not win them back. Upload one product photo and get a retargeting video that brings the item back with the specific detail a returning buyer is still weighing, so your remarketing audience gets a reason to finish the order.
benefits_h2: Why make retargeting video ads with AI?

benefits.t: Give viewed products a second reason to buy
benefits.d: The clip revisits one detail, such as an ear cushion, a pocket or a seam, that a returning shopper may still be weighing. It turns a reminder into an answer instead of repeating the same product shot.

benefits.t: Fresh creative without a second shoot
benefits.d: Run a routine version and a close-detail version from the same source photo, then test which proof earns the second look. New remarketing creative costs only credits, not another filming day.
Use 1:1 in feed placements and 9:16 in Reels, with clips at 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds. A short reminder works for cart audiences, while a longer clip can answer a hesitancy in full.

benefits.t: Audience facts stay in your platform
benefits.d: Add the offer, price, audience and frequency in your ad platform and keep claims about browsing history out of the scene. Downloads carry no AIVideosUGC watermark and can be used in your own paid ads.

intro: The sample shows an adult commuter using dark navy over-ear headphones during a train-station routine. It is an AI-generated scene, not a claim about an individual shopper or their past activity.
Pair a product reminder with an audience, offer, and frequency you configure in your ad platform. The scene itself does not identify visitors or cart activity.

A second-look ad should answer the detail a returning shopper may still be weighing. Show the headphones on a commute, the ear cushion in a creator review, or the shoe tread on the path where it is used. The scene works because the product returns to view with a reason, not because it claims to know who visited your store.

Keep the audience, offer, price, and frequency in the ad platform. In the creative, use one close action such as turning an ear cup, opening a pocket, tightening a lace, or checking a seam. End with the product held still so an editable reminder and a destination link can be added without covering the feature.

Check the reminder against the live product page before you launch. The color, version, and feature shown in the clip must match the item a shopper will receive, and any current offer must be added outside the generated frame. Test a routine scene against a detail scene while holding the audience and product page constant so the result tells you which proof earns the second look.
tip: Describe a quiet second-look action and leave the audience, price, and reminder wording to the ad platform and your editor.
steps_h2: How to make a retargeting video ad in 3 simple steps
steps_lead: Three steps turn one product photo into a second-look clip — no shoot, no new audience data, no repeated creative.

steps.d: Use a clear product image that gives the clip a recognizable shape and a detail worth revisiting.
Write a short moment, such as inspecting the ear cups before packing the headphones away. The return-to-product scene is generated without a shoot.
Add your offer and product page, then choose visitors, cart users and frequency in your ad platform. The file has no AIVideosUGC watermark.

ideas.d: Use one close action to bring a specific product detail back into view.
Show a product going into a bag, case, or drawer to suggest a next step without a promise.
Make another run that shows the same product from an angle the first clip did not cover.

faq.q: Does AIVideosUGC choose my retargeting audience?
faq.a: No. Set visitors, cart users, exclusions, budget, frequency, and delivery in your ad platform.

faq.q: Can the video claim that someone viewed or abandoned a cart?
faq.a: Do not make that claim in the generated scene. It does not know a viewer’s history. Add only text that matches your actual campaign and data.

faq.q: Will it add the offer or price?
faq.a: No. Add the current offer, price, dates, and disclosure in your editor or ad platform.

faq.q: Who actually sees the retargeting ad?
faq.a: You configure the audience, offer, and frequency in your ad platform. The video only supplies the return-to-product creative.

faq.q: Can the video identify returning shoppers?
faq.a: No. It cannot show real visitor or cart data; your ad platform matches the audience to the impression.

faq.q: What length and cost work for retargeting?
faq.a: A 6- or 10-second reminder is usually enough and costs 24 or 40 credits.

faq.q: Can I create another retargeting video from the same source photo?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the dark navy headphones as the reference, then change one routine or camera move at a time. Check that the ear cups, controls, and fit match the physical item. Add the current offer, reminder, and product link after download so the second-look ad stays easy to update. Keep routine and detail versions tied to the same product variant so a returning shopper does not see a different color or control layout. If the offer or destination changes, recheck every exported variant against the same product page and color.

faq.q: Can I show the video only to people who left a cart?
faq.a: Yes, using your ad platform. Upload the finished clip to a cart or website-visitor audience, set exclusions and frequency there, and keep any reminder wording tied to what your campaign actually offers.

faq.q: Should the retargeting clip say "you forgot this"?
faq.a: Only if your campaign supports that message, and add it as text outside the generated scene. The clip itself cannot know a viewer's history, so avoid personal claims and focus on bringing the product detail back into view.

visual.overview: A retargeting video gives the product another clear moment in a feed or product page. Show how it fits a routine or make one product detail easy to see. Use this format when shoppers need to bring dark navy headphones back with a specific reminder about fit, controls, or comfort. Keep one second-look detail visible from the first frame, then leave room for the offer and product link you add after download. Review the ear cups, controls, and color against your source before publishing. A returning shopper should see the product detail they may still be weighing before the reminder, offer, and destination compete for space.
